sheets.title: Indus Valley (Harappan) civilisation
sheets.intro: Every Harappan fact: phases, sites, town plan, trade, seals, faith, decline.

keys.name: Phases and dates

rows.v: 2600 – 1900 BCE (new NCERT); 2500 – 1750 BCE (R.S. Sharma, old NCERT)
Bronze Age / Chalcolithic – copper, bronze, gold, silver, tin, lead; NO iron
Harappan culture (first site dug); Indus-Sarasvati civilisation
One of the first three civilisations with Egypt and Mesopotamia

traps: Use the date range the options use: 2600 – 1900 or 2500 – 1750

rows.v: Sindh (Khairpur); F.A. Khan 1955; fortified town, "Kot Dijian" culture
Sindh; N.G. Majumdar 1929; pre-Harappan layers under Harappan ones
N Rajasthan (Ghaggar); A. Ghosh 1950 – 53; Sothi pottery
Haryana (Fatehabad); L.S. Rao 2003 – 06; claimed oldest Harappan layers; "dancing girl" on a potsherd

keys.name: Discovery

rows.v: First saw Harappa; took it for "Sangala" of Alexander's time
First DG of ASI (1861), "father of Indian archaeology"; 1875 noted Harappa bricks taken for railway ballast
DG ASI 1944; layer-wise digging at Harappa 1947; Aryan invasion theory

traps: Marshall announced (1924); Masson first saw; Sahni dug Harappa; Banerjee dug Mohenjo-daro

rows.v: About 13 lakh sq km – bigger than Egypt and Mesopotamia
About 1,500; Gujarat has the most in India
Daimabad (Maharashtra, Pravara); older books say Bhagatrav or Malwan
Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra (dried; linked with Sarasvati)
Type site; two rows of six granaries; workers’ quarters; Cemetery R-37 and Cemetery H; red sandstone male torso; bullock carts; coffin burial

keys.name: Mohenjo-daro

rows.v: Great Bath; Great Granary; assembly hall; college building; Pashupati seal; bronze Dancing Girl; "Priest-King" (steatite); unicorn seal; woven cotton
"Mound of the Dead"; largest site in Pakistan (c. 125 ha)

traps: Great Bath, Dancing Girl and Priest-King are all Mohenjo-daro, never Harappa

rows.v: Bead-making, shell, metal, seal and weight workshops; only city without a citadel; inkpot, lipstick; dog chasing a cat paw prints on a brick
Tidal dockyard (only port with dock); bead factory; Persian Gulf seal; rice husk; fire altars; double burial; ivory scale; accurate weights; chess-like game
National Maritime Heritage Complex being built
Khadir Bet, Rann of Kutch, Gujarat
Three-part city (citadel, middle, lower town); stone water reservoirs; stadium; signboard of 10 large signs

keys.name: Kalibangan

rows.v: A. Ghosh 1953; B.B. Lal, B.K. Thapar 1960 – 69
Ploughed field (criss-cross furrows, two crops, pre-Harappan); fire altars; symbolic burials; bangles; earthquake traces; wooden drain; bronze bull

traps: Ploughed field = Kalibangan; terracotta plough = Banawali

keys.name: Rakhigarhi

rows.v: Largest Harappan site now; burnt-brick houses, drains; mud-brick granary; alligator seal; 2019 ancient-DNA study

traps: Largest Harappan site = Rakhigarhi, not Dholavira or Mohenjo-daro

rows.v: Terracotta toy plough; good barley; fortified town; radial streets; cotton
First Harappan site dug after Independence; dog buried with master
Bones reported as horse (debated); pot burial; fort
Rice husk; Late Harappan "Rangpur culture"; Lustrous Red Ware

Desalpur (Kutch, P.P. Pandya 1963 – fort); Nageshwar (near Dwarka – shell bangles); Shikarpur (Kutch – shell, carnelian drills); Bhagatrav (Bharuch, Kim estuary – small port, beads); Bagasra (V.H. Sonawane 1996 – shell); Rojdi (Bhadar, Possehl 1982 – farm village)
Southernmost site; bronze hoard – chariot with two oxen, elephant, rhino, buffalo
Westernmost site; fortified trade post near the Arabian Sea; link to Mesopotamia
Balakot – shell work, Gulf trade; Allahdino – small unfortified village (1.4 ha)

keys.name: Shortughai

rows.v: Trading colony near lapis lazuli mines; only site with irrigation canals

traps: Irrigation canals only at Shortughai, not in Punjab or Sindh

rows.v: Ahar-Banas Chalcolithic of Harappan times; earliest leprosy skeleton in India
Grid – roads cross at right angles
Raised citadel (west – granaries, halls, offices) + lower town (east – houses, workers)
Burnt bricks of fixed ratio 4 : 2 : 1 (length : breadth : thickness)
Doors on side lanes, no windows to main street; wells, bathing floors
Covered house drains to street drains; cesspits; some street drains laid before houses
Watertight tank on the Mohenjo-daro citadel – only there
Same plan over a huge area – a strong central authority

keys.name: Economy and trade

rows.v: Wheat, barley (main); lentil, chickpea, sesame, mustard; millets (Gujarat); rice rare (Lothal, Rangpur); first cotton ("sindon" to Greeks)
Cattle, sheep, goat, buffalo, pig; NO cow on seals; horse absent or rare
Bull on seals → ox ploughing; terracotta plough (Banawali, Cholistan)
Weaving, beads (carnelian, jasper, steatite, faience, shell), metal, shell work
Copper – Khetri (Rajasthan); lapis lazuli – Afghanistan (Shortughai); gold from hoards

traps: Cow is not shown on Harappan seals

rows.v: Harappan seals and carnelian beads in Iraq; Persian Gulf seal at Lothal
By sea through the Persian Gulf; barter
Small weights binary – 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; big ones in 16s – 160, 200, 320, 640
Metal scale pans; accurate weights at Lothal; ivory scale at Lothal

keys.name: Seals and script

rows.v: Mostly steatite; also copper, gold, faience, ivory, terracotta
Mostly square; also oblong, round, triangular
Unicorn (one-horned bull) most common; bull, elephant, tiger, rhino; swastika on some
Pictographic; 375 – 400 signs (not alphabet); right to left, sometimes boustrophedon; longest text about 26 signs; NOT deciphered

traps: Script is undeciphered and not alphabetic

keys.name: Art and sculpture

rows.v: Bronze, lost-wax (cire perdue); tribhanga pose; Mohenjo-daro; now National Museum, Delhi
Steatite bust; trefoil shawl, half-shut eyes; Mohenjo-daro; now Karachi museum
Mother goddess, toys, carts, whistles, animals
Wheel-made; red with black designs (Red and Black ware)
Clay carts, dolls, rattles, marbles; gambling (dice)

traps: Dancing Girl = bronze; Priest-King = stone; both from Mohenjo-daro

rows.v: Horned, three-faced figure in yoga pose; elephant, tiger, rhino, buffalo around; two deer below; "proto-Shiva" (Marshall)
Peepal tree, horned bull, lingam and yoni stones, fire altars (Kalibangan, Lothal), Great Bath
Extended (north – south); symbolic, no body (Kalibangan); twin or joint (Lothal; man with dog at Ropar); pot burial (Surkotada)
Mostly secular – religion did not dominate
None proved; "palace" building had no rich finds
Name borrowed from Mesopotamia; not proved
Same bricks, weights, seals, pottery – some standard-setting authority
One state; many city rulers; or no single ruler
Cotton and wool; women – short skirt; men – long wrap
Women – bangles, necklaces of shell, gold, silver; men – amulets
Spindle whorls common – spun by hand at home
Wells and bath floors – care for water and cleanliness
Seals, script, weights, long trade, planned towns fade → villages (de-urbanisation)
Cemetery H (Punjab); Jhukar (Sindh); Rangpur (Gujarat); Bhagwanpura (Haryana – overlaps Painted Grey Ware)
Most sites left by c. 1800 BCE

keys.name: Decline theories
keys.hook: FAST-D: Flood, Aryans, Sarasvati, Tectonic, Disease

rows.v: Indus floods (M.R. Sahni, Lambrick); heavy rains
Mortimer Wheeler ("Indra stands accused") – not proved
Sarasvati drying from c. 1900 BCE; climate drier, cooler

traps: APPSC source dates the fall c. 1500 BCE; NCERT ends the urban phase c. 1900 BCE

rows.v: Chanhudaro, Kot Diji, Desalpur, Banawali, Surkotada
Absent or rare – main contrast with Rig Vedic people
Largest – Rakhigarhi; largest in Pakistan – Mohenjo-daro; first dug – Harappa 1921; first after Independence – Ropar; only dock – Lothal; stadium and signboard – Dholavira; no citadel – Chanhudaro
